_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution. `s.raster.raster` is a semio-NATIVE artifact carried in `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio`, so no third party can serve as its reference — see the noOracleDecision below. Note that the artifact is a LAYERED RASTER DOCUMENT, not an image file: the pixels live in referenced assets and the vocabulary edits the layer tree around them, so a PNG/TIFF/BMP crate is not a reference for it and registering one would be a category error.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: No third-party crate reads or writes semio's `.dsl.semio`/`.pack.semio` envelope, and the crates that DO read raster formats (`png`, `image`, `tiff`) read pixel containers — they are not authoritative over a layered document whose pixels sit behind ids in a root `assets` pool. What distinguishes this subset is that its layer nodes are three DIFFERENT kinds over one shared base: pixel layers carry an `assetIds` list, adjustment layers carry an `adjustmentKind` plus a parameter map, and group layers carry `children` — so `change-layer-adjustment-kind` applies to exactly one kind, `add-layer-asset`/`remove-layer-asset` join the layer tree to the root `assets` pool by id, and `reorder-layers` can lift a node OUT of a group rather than merely permute siblings. Confidence comes from the committed per-kind specification vectors under `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/<kind>/🧪️tests/<fixture>/`, already unit-tested inside the production crate, plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property. Two of those vectors are deliberately NEGATIVE — `add-layer-asset` records an accepted no-op and `remove-layer-asset` a `mutation.target-missing` rejection — so the `mutate-raster-1` case asserts the declared refusal for those kinds instead of pretending an application happened, and says so in its feature description.
